claim: Certain translational regulatory defects of the Drosophila oskar (osk) mRNA can be rescued in trans.
source: However, certain translational regulatory defects of the Drosophila oskar (osk) mRNA can be rescued in trans.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a key finding of the research.

claim: Inter-transcript interactions are promoted by assembly of mRNAs in particles.
source: We proposed that inter-transcript interactions, promoted by assembly of the mRNAs in particles, allow regulatory elements to act in trans.
evidence: This is the proposed model presented in the abstract.

claim: Disruption of PTB-dependent particle assembly inhibits rescue in trans.
source: Here we confirm predictions of that model and show that disruption of PTB-dependent particle assembly inhibits rescue in trans.
evidence: This is stated as a confirmed finding in the abstract.

claim: Regulation imposed by cis-acting elements embedded in the osk mRNA spreads to gurken mRNA.
source: Communication between transcripts is not limited to different osk mRNAs, as regulation imposed by cis-acting elements embedded in the osk mRNA spreads to gurken mRNA.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the abstract.

claim: Community effects exist in translational regulation.
source: We conclude that community effects exist in translational regulation.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract.

claim: PABP binds to the poly(A) tail at the 3' end of an mRNA.
source: For example, Poly(A) binding protein (PABP) binds to the poly(A) tail at the 3' end of an mRNA (Mangus et al., 2003)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Mangus et al., 2003.

claim: PABP enhances translation through its interaction with eIF4G.
source: Poly(A) binding protein (PABP) binds to the poly(A) tail at the 3' end of an mRNA (Mangus et al., 2003) and enhances translation through its interaction with eIF4G, a protein associated with the 5' cap of the mRNA (Tarun et al., 1997; Sonenberg and Dever, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Tarun et al., 1997 and Sonenberg and Dever, 2003.

claim: Many repressors of translation bind to elements in the 3' UTRs of mRNAs and interfere with the normal action of initiation factors at the 5' end of the mRNA.
source: Similarly, many repressors of translation bind to elements in the 3' untranslated regions (3' UTRs) of mRNAs and interfere with the normal action of initiation factors at the 5' end of the mRNA (Jackson et al., 2010; Gebauer and Hentze, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jackson et al., 2010 and Gebauer and Hentze, 2004.

claim: Long-range protein-protein interactions spanning the full length of mRNA are generally assumed to occur only in cis.
source: Such long-range protein-protein interactions, spanning the full length of the mRNA, are generally assumed to occur only in cis: PABP bound to the tail of one molecule of mRNA is expected to bind only the eIF4G associated with the other end of the same mRNA.
evidence: This is stated as a widespread assumption in the field.

claim: Inter-transcript interactions become more likely as the local density of mRNAs increases.
source: When mRNAs are dilute, intra-transcript interactions will predominate, but as the local density of mRNAs increases, inter-transcript interactions become more likely.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on concentration-dependent interactions.

claim: Control elements on one osk transcript can influence translation of another osk transcript.
source: Previously, we described an example involving the Drosophila oskar (osk) mRNA, in which control elements on one transcript influenced translation of another transcript (Reveal et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Reveal et al., 2010.

claim: osk mRNA is expressed during oogenesis and is subject to multiple forms of post-transcriptional control.
source: osk mRNA is expressed during oogenesis, and is subject to multiple forms of post-transcriptional control.
evidence: This is stated as background information about osk mRNA.

claim: osk mRNA is transported from nurse cells to the transcriptionally-silent oocyte.
source: Following transcription in the nurse cells of each egg chamber, osk mRNA is transported through cytoplasmic connections to the transcriptionally-silent oocyte.
evidence: This describes the localization pattern of osk mRNA.

claim: osk mRNA localizes to the posterior pole of the oocyte as oogenesis proceeds.
source: Eventually, as oogenesis proceeds, osk mRNA localizes to the posterior pole of the oocyte, and only then does Osk protein begin to accumulate.
evidence: This describes the temporal and spatial regulation of osk mRNA.

claim: Translation of osk mRNA is highly regulated with repression preventing premature translation from unlocalized mRNA.
source: Translation of osk mRNA is highly regulated: repression prevents premature translation from unlocalized mRNA, and activation turns on translation of the localized mRNA (Kim-Ha et al., 1995; Markussen et al., 1995; Rongo et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim-Ha et al., 1995; Markussen et al., 1995; Rongo et al., 1995.

claim: Both repression and activation of osk mRNA translation rely on binding sites for Bruno (Bru).
source: Both types of regulation rely on binding sites for Bruno (Bru) (Reveal et al., 2010; Kim-Ha et al., 1995; Webster et al., 1997; Reveal et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Reveal et al., 2010; Kim-Ha et al., 1995; Webster et al., 1997; Reveal et al., 2011.

claim: BREs reside in two clusters (AB and C regions) near the opposite ends of the osk 3' UTR.
source: These sites, BREs and others, reside in two clusters - the AB and C regions - near the opposite ends of the 3' UTR (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: All the BREs contribute to translational repression of osk mRNA.
source: All the BREs contribute to translational repression (Kim-Ha et al., 1995)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kim-Ha et al., 1995.

claim: The C region BREs play a role in translational activation of osk mRNA.
source: the C region BREs also play a role in translational activation (Reveal et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Reveal et al., 2010.

claim: Defects in repression from mutation of all BREs in osk ABC BRE- can be rescued by the presence of another osk mRNA that cannot make Osk protein but has all regulatory elements intact.
source: Strikingly, defects in either repression (from mutation of all BREs in osk ABC BRE-) or activation (from mutation of the C BREs in osk C BRE-) can be rescued by the presence of another osk mRNA, one that itself cannot make Osk protein but has all regulatory elements intact (Reveal et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Reveal et al., 2010.

claim: Defects in activation from mutation of the C BREs in osk C BRE- can be rescued by the presence of another osk mRNA that cannot make Osk protein but has all regulatory elements intact.
source: Strikingly, defects in either repression (from mutation of all BREs in osk ABC BRE-) or activation (from mutation of the C BREs in osk C BRE-) can be rescued by the presence of another osk mRNA, one that itself cannot make Osk protein but has all regulatory elements intact (Reveal et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Reveal et al., 2010.

claim: Bru binds Cup, a protein that competes with eIF4G for binding to eIF4E.
source: Bru binds Cup, a protein that competes with eIF4G for binding to eIF4E, the 5' cap-binding protein.
evidence: This describes the molecular mechanism of Bru-mediated repression.

claim: Cup engagement of eIF4E at the expense of the eIF4E/eIF4G interaction blocks translation initiation.
source: Cup engagement of eIF4E at the expense of the eIF4E/eIF4G interaction blocks translation initiation (Nakamura et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nakamura et al., 2004.

claim: Assembly of osk mRNAs into ribonucleoprotein particles (RNPs) places the mRNAs in close proximity, facilitating inter-transcript interactions.
source: We hypothesized that assembly of osk mRNAs into ribonucleoprotein particles (RNPs) places the mRNAs in close proximity, thus increasing their concentration and facilitating inter-transcript interactions to allow 'regulation in trans' (Reveal et al., 2010).
evidence: This is the hypothesis proposed by the authors, with reference to Reveal et al., 2010.

claim: The rescuing (donor) mRNA should have the regulatory element that the rescued (recipient) mRNA lacks.
source: First, the rescuing (donor) mRNA should have the regulatory element that the rescued (recipient) mRNA lacks.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction of the regulation in trans model.

claim: Rescue in trans should extend to other forms of regulation that rely on long-range protein-protein interactions, not just Bru-specific regulation.
source: Second, rescue in trans should not be Bru-specific, but should extend to other forms of regulation that also rely on long-range protein-protein interactions.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction of the regulation in trans model.

claim: Rescue in trans depends on cis-acting osk mRNA elements and trans-acting proteins that mediate RNP assembly.
source: Finally, rescue in trans would depend on the cis-acting osk mRNA elements and trans-acting proteins that mediate RNP assembly.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction of the regulation in trans model.

claim: PTB binds osk mRNA to form RNPs in vitro.
source: PTB binds osk mRNA to form RNPs in vitro (Besse et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Besse et al., 2009.

claim: PTB mediates association of osk mRNAs in vivo.
source: PTB also mediates association of osk mRNAs in vivo, as shown by the effects of loss of PTB on hitchhiking (Besse et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Besse et al., 2009.

claim: Localization-competent osk mRNAs can assist other mRNAs in moving to the posterior pole of the oocyte through hitchhiking.
source: the phenomenon in which localization-competent osk mRNAs can assist other mRNAs in moving to the posterior pole of the oocyte (Hachet and Ephrussi, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hachet and Ephrussi, 2004.

claim: Bru mediates in vitro oligomerization of RNAs with an unusually high density of Bru binding sites.
source: Similarly, Bru mediates in vitro oligomerization of RNAs with an unusually high density of Bru binding sites and could also oligomerize osk mRNA in vivo (Chekulaeva et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chekulaeva et al., 2006.

claim: osk mRNA undergoes direct RNA dimerization, relying on a dimerization motif in the 3' UTR.
source: Finally, osk mRNA undergoes direct RNA dimerization, relying on a dimerization motif in the 3' UTR (Jambor et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Jambor et al., 2011.

claim: The oskM1R∆121–150 mutant lacks the start codon for Long Osk and has a 30 nt deletion in the 5' UTR for Short Osk.
source: The oskM1R∆121–150 mutant lacks the start codon for Long Osk and has a 30 nt deletion in the 5' UTR for Short Osk (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the mutations in the oskM1R∆121–150 mutant, with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The oskM1R∆121–150 mutant is largely defective in Short Osk protein production.
source: This mutant is largely defective in Short Osk protein production, in addition to making no Long Osk because of the M1R mutation (Kanke and Macdonald, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kanke and Macdonald, 2015.

claim: Coexpression with osk54 strongly rescues the activation defect of osk C BRE-.
source: Although coexpression with osk54 (a protein null mutant with a short DNA insertion, introducing a stop codon at the end of the first exon) (Kim-Ha et al., 1991) strongly rescues the activation defect of osk C BRE- (Figure 1B)
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B and supported by a citation to Kim-Ha et al., 1991.

claim: No significant rescue of the oskM1R∆121–150 activation defect was found when coexpressed with osk54.
source: no significant rescue of the oskM1R∆121–150 activation defect was found (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The oskM1R∆121–150 mutant is not sensitive to rescue in trans.
source: Therefore, the oskM1R∆121–150 mutant is not sensitive to rescue in trans.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Mutants osk3'977–981 and osk3'984–988 have almost no osk patterning activity and are strongly defective in Osk protein production.
source: Mutants osk3'977–981 and osk3'984–988 (numbering indicates position in the osk 3' UTR) have almost no osk patterning activity and are strongly defective in Osk protein production (Ryu and Macdonald, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ryu and Macdonald, 2015.

claim: Mutant osk3'1004–1008 had strongly reduced osk patterning activity.
source: Mutant osk3'1004–1008, in which an A-rich sequence is disrupted (Kanke et al., 2015)(Figure 1A), also had strongly reduced osk patterning activity (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B and supported by a citation to Kanke et al., 2015.

claim: The 977–980 and 984–988 mutations disrupt binding of BSF protein.
source: the 977–980 and 984–988 mutations disrupt binding of BSF protein (Ryu and Macdonald, 2015)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ryu and Macdonald, 2015.

claim: The sequence affected by mutation 1004–1008 is a binding site for Poly(A) binding protein (PABP).
source: while the sequence affected by mutation 1004–1008 is a binding site for Poly(A) binding protein (PABP) (Vazquez-Pianzola et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Vazquez-Pianzola et al., 2011.

claim: The patterning defects of osk3'977–981, osk3'984–988, and osk3'1004–1008 mutants were strongly rescued by coexpression of osk54 mRNA.
source: The patterning defects of all three of these mutants were strongly rescued by coexpression of osk54 mRNA (Figure 1B, [Ryu and Macdonald, 2015]).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B and supported by a citation to Ryu and Macdonald, 2015.

claim: An osk::GFP transgene bearing the osk3'1004–1008 mutation showed rescue in trans.
source: Similarly, a more direct assay of Osk protein expression, using an osk::GFP transgene bearing the osk3'1004–1008 mutation, showed rescue in trans (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Regulatory elements likely to engage in long-range interactions (those in the 3' UTR) are sensitive to rescue in trans.
source: regulatory elements likely to engage in long-range interactions (i.e. those in the 3' UTR) are sensitive to rescue in trans
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of regulatory mutants.

claim: A regulatory element positioned near the site of translational initiation and less likely to participate in a long-range interaction is not sensitive to rescue in trans.
source: while a regulatory element positioned near the site of translational initiation and thus less likely to participate in a long-range interaction is not.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of regulatory mutants.

claim: In oskM139L, the translation start codon for the Short Osk protein isoform is mutated.
source: In oskM139L, the translation start codon for the Short Osk protein isoform is mutated.
evidence: This describes the mutation in oskM139L.

claim: Short Osk is the isoform with embryonic patterning activity.
source: Because Short Osk is the isoform with embryonic patterning activity, oskM139L lacks that activity (Vanzo and Ephrussi, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Vanzo and Ephrussi, 2002.

claim: oskM139L strongly rescued the translational activation defect of osk C BRE- and restored normal embryonic patterning.
source: Like osk54, oskM139L strongly rescued the translational activation defect of osk C BRE- and restored normal embryonic patterning (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2A.

claim: oskM1R∆121–150 was an effective donor for rescue of the osk C BRE- mutant in trans.
source: Likewise, oskM1R∆121–150, the mutant whose regulatory defect is not rescued in trans, was an effective donor for rescue of the osk C BRE- mutant in trans (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Both oskM139L and oskM1R∆121–150 restored Osk::GFP protein expression to wild-type levels when used as donors for osk::GFP C BRE-.
source: Both oskM139L and oskM1R∆121–150 restored Osk::GFP protein expression to wild-type levels, just as with the osk54 donor (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2C.

claim: A variety of osk mutants can act as donors for rescue in trans.
source: These results, and others (below), show that a variety of osk mutants can act as donors for rescue in trans; this property is not unique to osk54.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Rescue by oskM1R∆121–150 is consistent with 'regulation in trans', as the oskM1R∆121–150 mRNA includes the regulatory element that the osk::GFP C BRE- mRNA lacks.
source: Furthermore, rescue by oskM1R∆121–150 is consistent with 'regulation in trans', as the oskM1R∆121–150 mRNA includes the regulatory element that the osk::GFP C BRE- mRNA lacks.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results in the context of the regulation in trans model.

claim: Little or no GFP signal was detected when osk C BRE- was used as the donor for osk::GFP C BRE-.
source: Although the activation defect of osk::GFP C BRE- was strongly rescued by osk54 (and by other donors with intact C region BREs; Figure 2C, below), little or no GFP signal was detected with osk C BRE- as the donor (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The UAS-GFP donor did not rescue the activation defect of osk C BRE-.
source: The UAS-GFP donor did not rescue the activation defect of osk C BRE- (Figure 2D, compare to Figure 2A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2D.

claim: A donor with the osk 3' UTR AB region provided no rescue of the osk C BRE- activation defect.
source: Similarly, the donor with the osk 3' UTR AB region provided no rescue.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experiment.

claim: A donor carrying the osk 3' UTR C region provided a low level of rescue of the osk C BRE- activation defect.
source: A donor carrying the osk 3' UTR C region, and thus the activation element mutated in the osk C BRE- recipient, provided a low level of rescue.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experiment.

claim: Rescue was increased when both the AB and C regions were present in the donor.
source: Rescue was increased when both the AB and C regions were present
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experiment.

claim: The highest level of rescue was obtained when the GFP mRNA included the entire osk 3' UTR.
source: and the highest level of rescue was obtained when the GFP mRNA included the entire osk 3' UTR.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experiment.

claim: The different levels of rescue cannot be attributed to differences in the amounts of the various donor mRNAs.
source: The different levels of rescue cannot be attributed to differences in the amounts of the various donor mRNAs (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The C region must be present to provide the missing translational activation element.
source: The C region must be present to provide the missing translational activation element
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Other Bru binding sites that do not contribute to activation (the AB region sites) are not sufficient for rescue.
source: while other Bru binding sites that do not contribute to activation (the AB region sites) are not sufficient.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The weak rescue from the C region alone is consistent with the notion that rescue requires both the missing element and sequences which mediate assembly of osk RNPs.
source: The weak rescue from the C region alone is consistent with the notion that rescue requires both the missing element and sequences which mediate assembly of osk RNPs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results.

claim: The C region by itself supports weak association of GFP-C mRNAs with osk C BRE- transcripts.
source: We suggest that by itself the C region supports weak association of GFP-C mRNAs with osk C BRE- transcripts
evidence: This is a suggested interpretation of the results.

claim: Association of GFP-C mRNAs with osk C BRE- transcripts is strengthened moderately by addition of the AB region and more strongly by addition of the full 3' UTR.
source: and this association is strengthened moderately by addition of the AB region and more strongly by addition of the full 3' UTR.
evidence: This is a suggested interpretation of the results.

claim: Direct osk mRNA dimerization requires a RNA element which is deleted in mutant osk3'∆665–685.
source: Direct osk mRNA dimerization requires a RNA element (Jambor et al., 2011), which is deleted in mutant osk3'∆665–685 (labeled as dimer- in Figure 3).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Jambor et al., 2011 and shown in Figure 3.

claim: PTB-binding sites are spread throughout the osk mRNA 3' UTR.
source: These sites are spread throughout the osk mRNA 3' UTR (as shown by RNA binding assays), although individual sites have not been defined (Besse et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Besse et al., 2009.

claim: The binding specificity of Drosophila PTB is likely to be very similar or identical to that of the highly conserved mammalian homolog.
source: However, because the binding specificity of Drosophila PTB is likely to be very similar or identical to that of the highly conserved mammalian homolog, for which binding sites have been characterized by a combination of approaches (Pérez et al., 1997; Xue et al., 2009), candidate sites can be identified (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Pérez et al., 1997 and Xue et al., 2009, with candidate sites shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: PT mutations disrupt PTB binding to the osk 3' UTR.
source: When the competitor RNA included the PT mutations (3'PTmut), competition was less effective, demonstrating that the mutations do affect PTB-binding sites.
evidence: This is shown by the UV crosslinking competition binding assay results.

claim: The wild-type donor provides strong rescue of activation of osk::GFP C BRE-.
source: The wild-type donor provides strong rescue of activation, as does the donor lacking the dimerization motif (dimer-)(Figure 3E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The donor lacking the dimerization motif (dimer-) provides strong rescue of activation of osk::GFP C BRE-.
source: The wild-type donor provides strong rescue of activation, as does the donor lacking the dimerization motif (dimer-)(Figure 3E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The osk3'PTmut and osk3'PTmut dimer- donors provided almost no rescue of activation of osk::GFP C BRE-.
source: By contrast, the osk3'PTmut and osk3'PTmut dimer- donors provided almost no rescue of activation.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experiment.

claim: Some oocytes had trace levels of posterior GFP with the osk3'PTmut donor, while none were above background with the osk3'PTmut dimer- donor.
source: Although no statistically significant difference between GFP levels with these latter two donors was detected, some oocytes had trace levels with the osk3'PTmut donor, while none were above background with the osk3'PTmut dimer- donor, consistent with an additive effect of the two types of mutations (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The loss of rescue in trans cannot be attributed to failure of the donor mRNAs to localize to the posterior pole of the oocyte.
source: The loss of rescue in trans cannot be attributed to failure of the donor mRNAs to localize to the posterior pole of the oocyte, as the PT mutations do not interfere with posterior localization (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: Each subset of PT mutations reduced PTB binding to short segments of the osk mRNA 3' UTR.
source: To confirm that each subset of PT mutations reduced PTB binding, short segments of the osk mRNA 3' UTR containing the subsets of mutations were tested in UV crosslinking assays. Each of the four 3' UTR segments bound PTB, and for each the binding was substantially lower when the RNA contained the PT mutations (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Each of the donor transgenes with subsets of PT mutations was impaired for rescue of the translational activation defect of the osk::GFP C BRE- recipient.
source: Each of these donors was impaired for rescue of the translational activation defect of the osk::GFP C BRE- recipient, although none was as defective as the osk3'PTmut donor (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The PT mutations had an additive effect on rescue in trans.
source: Thus, the PT mutations had an additive effect, and some subsets of the mutations inhibited rescue in trans more than others.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The differences in rescuing activity did not correlate with the amounts of the different donor mRNAs.
source: The differences in rescuing activity did not correlate with the amounts of the different donor mRNAs (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The osk 3' UTR RNA with the 3'375–540 subset of PT mutations was the weakest competitor for PTB binding.
source: Notably, among this group, the osk 3' UTR RNA with the 3'375–540 subset of PT mutations was the weakest competitor, just as the osk3'375–540 PTmut transgene was the least effective donor for rescue in trans.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the competition-binding assays.

claim: A correlation exists between strength of PTB binding and strength of rescue in trans.
source: Thus, we did observe a correlation between strength of PTB binding and strength of rescue in trans.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Reducing the level of PTB activity in heph heterozygotes impaired rescue of the translation activation defect of osk::GFP C BRE-.
source: Reducing the level of PTB activity in the heph heterozygotes impaired rescue of the translation activation defect, causing a lower level of Osk::GFP.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experiment.

claim: Reducing the level of PTB activity had no effect on Osk::GFP levels when using a recipient mRNA with no translation defect (osk::GFP).
source: By contrast, in a control experiment using a recipient mRNA with no translation defect, osk::GFP, reducing the level of PTB activity had no effect on Osk::GFP levels (Figure 4F, left).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4F.

claim: PTB-dependent assembly of osk mRNA into RNPs is required for rescue in trans.
source: Thus, the results of both kinds of tests to determine the role of PTB - mutating candidate PTB-binding sites or reducing PTB activity - point to the same conclusion: PTB-dependent assembly of osk mRNA into RNPs is required for rescue in trans, supporting the model of 'regulation in trans'.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: gurken (grk) mRNA is one of the most highly enriched for candidate PTB-binding sites among ovarian mRNAs.
source: Among ovarian mRNAs, one of the most highly enriched for candidate PTB-binding sites is gurken (grk) (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Supplementary file 1.

claim: PTB associates with grk mRNA, both in vitro and in vivo.
source: Furthermore, PTB associates with grk mRNA, both in vitro and in vivo (McDermott et al., 2012; McDermott and Davis, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to McDermott et al., 2012 and McDermott and Davis, 2013.

claim: grk mRNA is highly enriched in the oocyte during previtellogenic stages.
source: Notably, grk mRNA is, like osk, highly enriched in the oocyte during previtellogenic stages (Figure 5A,B) (Neuman-Silberberg and Schüpbach, 1993).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5A,B and supported by a citation to Neuman-Silberberg and Schüpbach, 1993.

claim: At stage 8, both grk and osk mRNAs align at the anterior margin of the oocyte.
source: Later, at stage 8, both mRNAs align at the anterior margin of the oocyte, but then go their separate ways within the oocyte: grk becomes restricted to the anterodorsal corner, while osk moves to the posterior (Kim-Ha et al., 1991; Neuman-Silberberg and Schüpbach, 1993; Ephrussi et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim-Ha et al., 1991; Neuman-Silberberg and Schüpbach, 1993; Ephrussi et al., 1991.

claim: grk and osk mRNAs have similar distributions for part of oogenesis and have the potential to reside in the same RNPs during that period.
source: Thus, grk and osk mRNAs have similar distributions for part of oogenesis and have the potential to reside in the same RNPs during that period.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the localization patterns.

claim: Translation of osk mRNA is strongly repressed for the entire period of shared localization with grk mRNA.
source: Because translation of osk mRNA is strongly repressed for the entire period of shared localization, the most likely trans effect is for osk mRNA to confer some degree of translational repression on grk mRNA.
evidence: This is stated as a logical inference.

claim: When only osk3'PTmut mRNA was present, Grk protein levels were higher than when osk+ mRNA was also present.
source: Remarkably, the type of osk mRNA present did affect Grk protein levels. When only osk3'PTmut mRNA was present, Grk protein levels were higher than when osk+ mRNA was also present (Figure 5I).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5I.

claim: No change in Grk protein levels was found when using an osk transgene that is a strong donor for rescue of osk mRNA regulatory defects.
source: As a control, we performed the same type of experiment with an osk transgene that is a strong donor for rescue of osk mRNA regulatory defects and found no change in Grk protein levels (Figure 5H).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5H.

claim: The differing behaviors of the osk3'PTmut and osk control transgenes cannot be attributed to differences in mRNA levels.
source: The differing behaviors of the osk3'PTmut and osk control transgenes cannot be attributed to differences in mRNA levels (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5G.

claim: None of the osk mRNAs in the Grk protein level experiments produce any Osk protein at previtellogenic stage 5/6.
source: Importantly, none of the osk mRNAs in these experiments produce any Osk protein at these stages of oogenesis (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5E,F.

claim: osk mRNA, not Osk protein, influences Grk expression.
source: Therefore, we conclude that osk mRNA, not Osk protein, influences Grk expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The increase in Grk levels when osk mRNA is impaired in PTB-dependent RNP assembly is consistent with the strong translational repression of osk mRNAs acting in trans to confer some degree of translational repression on grk mRNAs present in the same RNPs.
source: The increase in Grk levels when osk mRNA is impaired in PTB-dependent RNP assembly is consistent with the strong translational repression of osk mRNAs acting in trans to confer some degree of translational repression on grk mRNAs present in the same RNPs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results.

claim: The IBE sequence is UUUAY (Y is pyrimidine).
source: The IBE sequence - UUUAY (Y is pyrimidine) - was identified as a binding site for Imp protein (Munro et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Munro et al., 2006.

claim: Thirteen copies of the IBE appear in the osk mRNA, all in the 3' UTR.
source: Thirteen copies of the IBE appear in the osk mRNA, all in the 3' UTR.
evidence: This describes the distribution of IBEs in osk mRNA.

claim: Three of the IBE mutants (subsets A, C and D) fail to accumulate Osk despite having normal localization of osk mRNA.
source: Three of the mutants (subsets A, C and D; Figure 6C) fail to accumulate Osk despite having normal localization of osk mRNA
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: The fourth IBE mutant (subset B) has normal Osk expression.
source: while the fourth mutant (subset B) has normal Osk expression.
evidence: This is stated as a result.

claim: Mutating the A, C, or D subsets of IBEs disrupts colocalization of Imp protein with osk mRNA at the posterior pole of stage 9/10 oocytes.
source: Mutating the A, C, or D subsets of IBEs disrupts colocalization of Imp protein with osk mRNA at the posterior pole of stage 9/10 oocytes, supporting the notion that Imp binds osk mRNA through these elements and mediates activation of osk mRNA translation (Munro et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Munro et al., 2006.

claim: Mutants lacking Imp protein have normal osk expression.
source: However, mutants lacking Imp protein have normal osk expression, suggesting that the IBEs also bind another factor, with this second factor contributing to activation of osk translation (Munro et al., 2006; Geng and Macdonald, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Munro et al., 2006 and Geng and Macdonald, 2006.

claim: The osk IBE- mutant was not strongly rescued in trans.
source: Previously, we found that the osk IBE- mutant was not strongly rescued in trans (Reveal et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Reveal et al., 2010.

claim: Neither of two transgenes with mutated IBEs strongly rescued the translational activation defect of the osk C BRE- mutant.
source: Neither of two transgenes with mutated IBEs strongly rescued the translational activation defect of the osk C BRE-mutant (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Neither IBE mutant restored protein expression of the osk::GFP C BRE- mutant.
source: Similarly, neither IBE mutant restored protein expression of the osk::GFP C BRE- mutant (Figure 6F, data not shown).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Failure to rescue strongly was not due to insufficient mRNA, as both IBE mutant osk mRNAs were present at high levels.
source: Failure to rescue strongly was not due to insufficient mRNA, as both IBE mutant osk mRNAs were present at high levels (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Mutation of the IBEs disrupted rescue in trans, with the mutant osk mRNAs unable to act as either donor or recipient.
source: Thus, mutation of the IBEs disrupted rescue in trans, with the mutant osk mRNAs unable to act as either donor or recipient.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The osk 11-13- mutant had normal Osk accumulation.
source: Notably, the osk 11-13- mutant had normal Osk accumulation (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The osk 3'∆83–116 mutant had normal Osk accumulation.
source: Again, this mutant is expected to more strongly disrupt Imp/unknown binding than the corresponding osk IBE- mutant, but it had normal Osk accumulation (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The original IBE mutations appear to disrupt translational activation of osk mRNA not by removing a binding site, but by creating a novel type of element.
source: Thus, the original IBE mutations appear to disrupt translational activation of osk mRNA not by removing a binding site, but by creating a novel type of element, such as a binding site for another factor.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Both osk 3'∆83–116 and osk 11-13- mutants strongly rescued translational activation of osk::GFP C BRE-.
source: By contrast, both osk 3'∆83–116 and osk 11-13- mutants strongly rescued translational activation (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The gain-of-function property of the original IBE- mutations not only disrupts osk mRNA translation, but also interferes with the ability of the mRNA to participate in rescue in trans.
source: It seems likely, then, that the gain-of-function property of the original IBE- mutations not only disrupts osk mRNA translation, but also interferes with the ability of the mRNA to participate in rescue in trans.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Long-range interactions involving structures or factors associated with the different ends of an individual mRNA are required for translation.
source: Long-range interactions involving structures or factors associated with the different ends of an individual mRNA are required for translation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Inter-transcript interactions have generally not been considered in models of translation or its regulation.
source: Nevertheless, inter-transcript interactions have generally not been considered in models of translation or its regulation.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about the field.

claim: The work establishes parameters for rescue in trans.
source: The work described here establishes parameters for this rescue in trans
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the work.

claim: Conditions which reduce RNP assembly diminish rescue in trans.
source: shows that conditions which reduce RNP assembly diminish rescue in trans
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the work.

claim: Regulation imposed on the osk mRNA influences the expression of grk mRNA by a trans effect.
source: and provides evidence that regulation imposed on the osk mRNA influences the expression of grk mRNA by a similar trans effect.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the work.

claim: The results are fully consistent with and lend considerable support to the model of 'regulation in trans'.
source: Our results are fully consistent with and lend considerable support to the model of 'regulation in trans'.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion.

claim: Mutations affecting long-range regulatory interactions should be susceptible to rescue in trans.
source: In the context of the proposed model, mutations affecting long-range regulatory interactions should be susceptible to rescue in trans, while other types of regulatory defects would not.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction of the model.

claim: Three mutants with mutations in the 3' UTR could be rescued in trans.
source: Testing new regulatory mutants as recipients, we found that three mutants with mutations in the 3' UTR could be rescued in trans
evidence: This is stated as a result of testing new mutants.

claim: A mutant with defects in the 5' region of the mRNA could not be rescued in trans.
source: while a mutant with defects in the 5' region of the mRNA could not.
evidence: This is stated as a result of testing new mutants.

claim: Sensitivity of the 3' UTR regulatory elements to rescue in trans is consistent with their participation in long-range interactions to activate translation.
source: Sensitivity of the 3' UTR regulatory elements to rescue in trans is consistent with their participation in long-range interactions to activate translation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results.

claim: The osk3'1004–1008 mutant is defective in an A-rich element, which likely serves to bind PABP.
source: In particular, the osk3'1004–1008 mutant is defective in an A-rich element, which likely serves to bind PABP (Vazquez-Pianzola et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Vazquez-Pianzola et al., 2011.

claim: PABP interacts with the translation initiation factor eIF4G associated with the mRNA 5' cap, and this interaction has the potential to occur between different transcripts.
source: PABP interacts with the translation initiation factor eIF4G (Tarun et al., 1997), associated with the mRNA 5' cap, and this interaction has the potential to occur between different transcripts.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Tarun et al., 1997 and is stated as a logical inference.

claim: The element missing from the recipient must be provided by the donor.
source: First, we find that the element missing from the recipient must be provided by the donor, as predicted by the model of 'regulation in trans' [but also consistent with other models - see (Wilusz and Wilusz, 2010)].
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from experiments, with a citation to Wilusz and Wilusz, 2010.

claim: Although the missing element is required in the donor, it is not sufficient, and additional 3' UTR sequences must be present to obtain a substantial degree of rescue.
source: Second, although the missing element is required in the donor, it is not sufficient, and additional 3' UTR sequences must be present to obtain a substantial degree of rescue.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from experiments.

claim: Many osk mRNAs can act as donors for rescue in trans; this appears to be the default property.
source: Third, many osk mRNAs can act as donors for rescue in trans; this appears to be the default property.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from experiments.

claim: Even if an osk mRNA is not receptive to rescue in trans, this does not exclude the possibility that it can act as a donor.
source: Even if an osk mRNA is not receptive to rescue in trans, this does not exclude the possibility that it can act as a donor.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from experiments.

claim: There are mutations which interfere with the ability of an osk mRNA to act as a donor for rescue in trans.
source: Fourth, there are mutations which interfere with the ability of an osk mRNA to act as a donor for rescue in trans.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from experiments.

claim: The original IBE mutations appear to cause a dominant gain-of-function defect, perhaps by serendipitous formation of a binding site for an unknown factor.
source: Thus, the original IBE mutations appear to cause a dominant gain-of-function defect, perhaps by serendipitous formation of a binding site for an unknown factor.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results.

claim: Bound Bru could occlude binding of the unknown factor to the B group IBEs, thus avoiding the adverse effects.
source: We suggest that bound Bru could occlude binding of the unknown factor, thus avoiding the adverse effects.
evidence: This is stated as a suggested explanation.

claim: Mutants designed to disrupt RNP assembly fail to rescue in trans.
source: Finally, mutants designed to disrupt RNP assembly also fail to rescue in trans.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from experiments.

claim: Mutation of many PTs in the donor mRNA most dramatically disrupted rescue in trans.
source: Mutation of many PTs in the donor mRNA most dramatically disrupted rescue in trans, with lesser defects from mutating subsets of these PTs.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from experiments.

claim: The additive nature of the PT mutations is fully consistent with the notion that they serve as binding sites for PTB.
source: The additive nature of the PT mutations is fully consistent with the notion that they serve as binding sites for PTB, which assembles osk mRNA into RNPs in vitro and is required for association of osk mRNAs in vivo (Besse et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation, with a citation to Besse et al., 2009.

claim: Lowering the activity of PTB diminished rescue of the translational activation defect, leading to a lower level of Osk protein.
source: Consistent with 'regulation in trans', lowering the activity of PTB diminished rescue of the translational activation defect, leading to a lower level of Osk protein.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experiment.

claim: PTB is implicated in translational repression of osk mRNA.
source: PTB is implicated in translational repression of osk mRNA (Besse et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Besse et al., 2009.

claim: A reduced level of PTB could influence Osk protein levels more directly through reduced efficiency of repression.
source: and so a reduced level of PTB could also influence Osk protein levels more directly. However, a lower efficiency of repression would increase, not lower, the level of Osk protein
evidence: This is stated as a logical inference.

claim: The effect of reduced PTB on Osk protein levels is more reasonably attributed to 'regulation in trans'.
source: and the effect we observe is more reasonably attributed to 'regulation in trans'.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results.

claim: Almost any mRNA should be susceptible to inter-transcript interactions influencing its translation.
source: By the model of 'regulation in trans', almost any mRNA should be susceptible to inter-transcript interactions influencing its translation.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction of the model.

claim: Such effects would be most likely for mRNAs in close proximity to one another, either because of an overall high mRNA concentration or because of coassembly in RNPs.
source: In practice, such effects would be most likely for mRNAs in close proximity to one another, either because of an overall high mRNA concentration or because of coassembly in RNPs.
evidence: This is stated as a logical inference.

claim: Removing candidate PTB-binding sites from osk mRNA led to elevation of Grk protein levels early in oogenesis.
source: Remarkably, removing candidate PTB-binding sites from osk mRNA led to elevation of Grk protein levels early in oogenesis.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experiment.

claim: Association of the osk and grk mRNAs could lead to some degree of translational repression of grk.
source: Because translation of osk mRNA is strongly repressed at this developmental stage, association of the osk and grk mRNAs could lead to some degree of translational repression of grk.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results.

claim: Disrupting association of osk and grk mRNAs would reduce repression of grk, leading to higher Grk protein levels.
source: Disrupting this association would reduce repression of grk, leading to higher Grk protein levels, as we observed.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results.

claim: The absence of other reports of trans effects in translational regulation may be misleading, as detecting trans effects is not straightforward.
source: The absence of other reports of this phenomenon may be misleading, as detecting trans effects is not straightforward.
evidence: This is stated as a discussion point.

claim: For osk mRNA, rescue in trans was discovered by comparing the effects of cis regulatory mutations in the presence or absence of other osk transcripts.
source: For osk mRNA, rescue in trans was discovered by comparing the effects of cis regulatory mutations in the presence or absence of other osk transcripts (Reveal et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Reveal et al., 2010.

claim: Several localized mRNAs are transported in RNPs containing a single mRNA molecule.
source: Curiously, several such mRNAs - but not osk - are transported in RNPs containing a single mRNA molecule (Batish et al., 2012; Amrute-Nayak and Bullock, 2012; Mikl et al., 2011; Little et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Batish et al., 2012; Amrute-Nayak and Bullock, 2012; Mikl et al., 2011; Little et al., 2015.

claim: Isolation of individual mRNAs may serve to ensure that 'regulation in trans' does not occur and that regulation is constrained to that imposed by embedded cis elements.
source: Perhaps, such isolation of individual mRNAs serves to ensure that 'regulation in trans' does not occur and that regulation is constrained to that imposed by embedded cis elements.
evidence: This is stated as a speculative interpretation.
